findings.quote: Revenue in the fiscal quarter ended July 4, 2026 was $888.6 million, up from $762.3 million in the same quarter a year earlier and $839.2 million in the prior quarter.
findings.issue: The prose correctly dated the reported quarter but the built report labelled it 'Q3'26' (snapshot rows and filing badge), colliding with catalysts[1] third-quarter guidance of $945-975M, so a reader saw two revenue figures both tagged Q3.
findings.fix: Add one clause anchoring the quarter ended July 4, 2026 as the company's second fiscal quarter (2Q 2026) so the guidance reads as the following quarter, and flag the vendor 'Q3'26' snapshot/badge mislabel to the desk.
findings.note: Still fixed on the current inputs. incomeCommentary opens 'Revenue in Vishay's second fiscal quarter, ended July 4, 2026' and reconciles the feed's Q3 label once; the Facts block still labels the quarter Q3'26 (ended 2026-07-04), so the reconciliation remains needed and accurate.

findings.quote: with the new German 12-inch fab aimed at higher-value power semiconductors.
findings.issue: Unsupported characterisation. The grounding surface describes the Itzehoe facility only as a 12-inch wafer fab being built adjacent to an existing 8-inch fab; neither the Facts nor Context state what it will produce, so 'aimed at higher-value power semiconductors' is an inference the pack does not make.
findings.fix: Drop the product claim and state only what the surface supports (a new 12-inch wafer fab in Itzehoe, Germany), or requalify to what is grounded.
findings.note: Still fixed. growth.points[1] reads '...with the new German 12-inch wafer fab adding internal capacity.' No other field reintroduces a product claim for the fab.

findings.quote: gross margin moves back toward the high-20s the company reached in 2021 and 2022
findings.issue: Imprecise and internally inconsistent. The income table shows FY22 gross margin of 30.3% (low-30s), which the durability section itself quotes, so 'high-20s ... in 2021 and 2022' understates the 2022 figure and clashes with the moat section.
findings.fix: Refer to the peak years accurately, e.g. 'toward the high-20s to low-30s reached in 2021 and 2022', or cite the 2022 peak of 30.3% as the upper reference.
findings.note: Still fixed. The driver reads 'gross margin moves back toward its 2021 and 2022 highs,' consistent with the unchanged income table (FY21 27.4%, FY22 30.3%).

findings.quote: free cash turned positive in the latest quarter, after two negative quarters, as earnings improved and spending moderated
findings.issue: Only one immediately-preceding quarter (ended April 4, 2026, -$46.9M) was negative; the other negative value on the surface is the year-ago quarter, not the quarter before April, so 'after two negative quarters' implies a consecutive streak the surface does not establish.
findings.fix: State only what the quarterly series supports, e.g. 'after the prior quarter's -$46.9 million outflow', or generalise to the FY25 negative free-cash run.
findings.note: Still fixed. cashflowCommentary reads 'reversing the prior quarter's outflow,' which matches the MD&A free-cash table (latest quarter $10,313 thousand, prior quarter $(46,926) thousand).

findings.quote: diluted EPS was {+ $0.19 +} against {+ $0.01 +} a year ago
findings.issue: Span misuse in two places. House style limits {+ +} to signed changes or explicit positives; wrapping the depressed year-ago base of $0.01 in a bullish span styles a weak comparison figure as a positive.
findings.fix: Keep the bullish span on the improved figure ({+ $0.19 +}) and leave the prior-year $0.01 unmarked in both fields.
findings.note: Still fixed in both fields; the year-ago $0.01 is unmarked.

findings.quote: The July equity raise diluted shareholders. Issuing 17.25 million shares strengthened the balance sheet but increased the share count against which future earnings are measured.
findings.issue: Repetition across sections. balanceCommentary already introduced the raise with the same 17.25 million share figure and the same dilution point, and the risks bullet restated it in different words rather than referring back.
findings.fix: Refer back to the July raise in words and make a distinct point, or drop the restated 17.25 million figure already established in balanceCommentary.
findings.note: Still fixed. The dilution bullet is gone; the raise and its dilution are stated once, in balanceCommentary.

findings.quote: Price-to-sales is 1.5x, and EV/EBITDA is not meaningful on depressed trailing EBITDA.
findings.issue: The rebuilt Facts now carry a trailing EV/EBITDA of 17.4x (Snapshot 'EV/EBITDA (TTM): 17.4x' and the Multiples row 'EV/EBITDA: 17.4x'), and data/vsh.json renders 17.446 in both the snapshot and the multiples table. The sentence was written when that cell was blank; it now contradicts a figure printed on the same page. The claim is also unsupported on the new surface: the 'near-zero denominator' reasoning the paragraph applies to the 174.4x P/E does not carry over, because 17.4x is an ordinary multiple, not one inflated by a vanishing denominator. The gap between 174.4x trailing earnings and 17.4x trailing EBITDA is itself informative (earnings are thin after depreciation, interest and tax, while EBITDA is not), and the paragraph skips it.
findings.fix: Quote the trailing EV/EBITDA of 17.4x and read it for the holder: say what it shows next to the 174.4x trailing P/E, and that trailing EBITDA still sits near the cycle trough (FY24 and FY25 EBITDA of $0.2 billion and $0.3 billion against $0.6 to $0.8 billion in FY21 to FY23), and reach a view on what the multiple means. Do not compute a forward EV/EBITDA, and keep the rest of the paragraph unchanged.
findings.note: Fixed. multiplesCommentary now quotes trailing EV/EBITDA of 17.4x, explains the gap to the 174.4x P/E in words, places the EBITDA base near the cycle low with figures that match the income table (FY24 0.2, FY25 0.3 vs FY21-FY23 0.6-0.8, in billions), and reaches a view: a multiple on trough EBITDA, neither cheap nor dear, that compresses with the same recovery the forward P/E prices. No new figure is computed and nothing repeats another section.
